objective: Gate calm water total resistance coefficient, plus sinkage and trim, for the KRISO Container Ship at model scale against the Tokyo 2015 workshop's own tabulated experimental data at three Froude numbers on two mesh rungs, with the measurement definition pinned contractually before any solve in the manner the F7a re-gate specification establishes
rationale: KCS is the strongest reference data position of the four naval cases considered, and that is a measured finding rather than an assumption. The Tokyo 2015 workshop resistance spreadsheet was parsed this session: six Froude numbers from 0.108 to 0.282 carrying total resistance coefficient, sinkage at forward and aft perpendiculars, mean sinkage and trim, fully open with no registration wall, model scale 1 to 31.59, length between perpendiculars 7.2786 metres, design Froude number 0.260, and the geometry verified downloadable from the bare host. Nothing needs digitising and nothing needs optical character recognition, which is true of neither the Wigley data nor the propeller reference. The machinery is present and verified: the installation ships two complete free surface container ship templates, one fixed and one moving, with automatic mesh generation, staged refinement passes, a force integration function object on the hull patch, and a rigid body motion dictionary carrying a composite heave plus pitch joint, which is exactly the pair a sinkage and trim case needs. Against that, two honest counterweights. First, configured is not active: this lab has never run a ship case, so the cost estimate has no measured anchor and is graded against the outturn per the charter's factor three rule. Second, the dam break ladder rule blocks the hull rungs behind a gate that still fails at plus 11.0 percent, and this proposal does not attempt to talk its way past that block. It is filed so the cost and the data position are on the record when Katie rules on the scoping question the F7 marine case record raises, namely whether a dry bed contact line failure should gate a wave making case at all
gate: Declared before any mesh exists. Reference: the Tokyo 2015 vary_Fr_2-1.xls experimental CT, sinkage and trim, with the exact sheet, row and column recorded in the pre-registration and the file hashed. Stations: three Froude numbers spanning the tabulated range and including the design point 0.260, frozen before the first solve. Metric definition pinned in the pre-registration on the F7a_REGATE_SPEC.md pattern: the force-averaging window and its transient-rejection rule, the wetted-surface reference area and whether it is static or instantaneous, the sinkage and trim sign convention and the reference points they are measured at, and the dynamic-pressure reference. Tolerance stated as a relative band on max deviation over the three stations, anchored to the workshop's own reported inter-facility scatter rather than chosen by this lab. Three-valued verdict per docket B2: PASS if max deviation over the three stations is inside the declared band on both mesh rungs and the fine rung is not worse than the coarse; FAIL, reported as a result, if outside with a settled force history; NO VERDICT if the force history fails its declared settling test on either rung, which is the outcome F8 actually returned on the nearest comparable stack and is therefore a live possibility rather than a formality
cost_basis: Estimate with an explicitly wide band and no measured anchor, because no ship case has ever run in this lab. Anchored to the shipped container ship template's own dimensions read from its dictionaries: a base mesh of 134,064 cells before snapping, an automatic mesh generation ceiling of two million cells, eight subdomains, and four thousand steps. Priced as six solves, three Froude numbers on two mesh rungs, at roughly 400 to 900 core minutes each, plus meshing. SCOPE NOTE, and Katie can buy less: the 3000 prices the FULL item. A feasibility first purchase, one coarse mesh at one Froude number with the wave pattern physics check only, is about 450 core minutes, and the launch prompt's hard stop at each stage boundary makes that smaller purchase a real option rather than a promise. Buying the 450 first and repricing the remainder against its measured outturn is the recommended route. Calibration caution carried deliberately: the nearest comparable item in this lab, the F8 rotor, cost 47.7 core minutes against its own estimate of 6, an eight times overrun, so this figure should be read as an order of magnitude and not as a bid. Graded against the measured cost afterwards per the charter's factor three rule
expected_knowledge_gain: Three distinguishable outcomes. A pass gives the lab its first ship scale free surface credential against open workshop data that naval engineers recognise on sight, and it establishes a measured cost basis for every subsequent hull, which no naval estimate currently has. A fail with settled forces is a real finding about free surface resistance at model scale and bounds what the marine line may claim. A no verdict on settling is the most valuable of the three at this stage, because it would show that the settling problem the F8 rotor hit on the steady stack also afflicts the free surface stack, which would redirect the whole marine line onto instrument work before any further hull is meshed
hard_criterion_note: New case with no existing family in this lab. The nearest relatives are F7a, which is 2-D dam break and fails its gate, and the DTCHull tutorial, which has never been run here. Hardness is therefore genuine and is the reason the proposal is staged and pre-registered rather than launched as one block
